message.content: The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  Roughly **23,000–24,000** soldiers on the Anglo‑Dutch‑Prussian side were killed, wounded or taken prisoner, while the French and their allies suffered about **25,000–26,000** casualties.  In total, the battle cost around **48,000–50,000** lives and injuries.
